instruction.text: Read the steps of a bee pollinating flowers and sort them into the correct order, with the first step at the top.

atoms.text: Bees are attracted to a flower by the brightly-coloured petals.
Bees land on the flower to drink nectar to make honey.
Pollen from the anther attaches to the hairs on the bees.
Bees move from flower to flower, carrying the pollen with them.

instruction.text: Read the steps of a bee pollinating flowers and sort them into the correct order, with the first step at the top.

atoms.text: When bees land on new flowers, the stigmas of the flowers will catch the pollen.
The pollen then travels down into the ovary.
In the ovary, the pollen fertilises the ovules, creating seeds.
The seeds can then be dispersed and grow into new plants.
